summary.name: TensorFlow Playground
summary.one_liner: An interactive browser visualization where you can tinker with a small neural network and watch it learn from toy datasets.
use_cases: teaching neural network concepts in a classroom
experimenting with network architecture on toy data
understanding how predictions and confidence are shown
summary.what_it_does: The page is a browser-based neural network playground for learning. Users can choose which features and controls are visible to tailor it to a lesson. Hidden-layer connections are colored by weight sign (blue positive, orange negative), and output points and background colors show the network's predictions and confidence. The page states it uses a small custom neural network library built for this visualization rather than TensorFlow itself. The project is open sourced on GitHub under the Apache License.
notable: Runs in the browser with color-coded weights, neurons and predictions shown live
Controls let educators show only selected features for a topic or lesson
Open sourced on GitHub under Apache License; built by Daniel Smilkov and Shan Carter, extending Andrej Karpathy's convnet.js demo
Uses a tiny custom neural network library, not TensorFlow itself
caveats: Uses a tiny custom library for education, so it is not meant for real-world applications; the page recommends TensorFlow for that
